```
def exact_entry_count(pattern_bounds, cap):
    if not pattern_bounds: return 0
    if cap <= 1:
        return cap if any(_key_count(b) > 0 for b in pattern_bounds) else 0
    by_len = defaultdict(list)
    for bounds in pattern_bounds:
        total = _key_count(bounds)
        if total == 0: continue
        if total >= cap: return cap
        by_len[len(bounds)].append((bounds, total))
    boxes = []
    for length, group in by_len.items():
        distinct = {}
        for bounds, total in group:
            key = tuple(tuple(p) for p in bounds)
            distinct[key] = (bounds, total)
        boxes.extend(_drop_contained(list(distinct.values())))
    boxes.sort(key=lambda item: -item[1])
    keys=set()
    for bounds,_ in boxes:
        axes=[_key_values(lo,hi) for lo,hi in bounds]
        for key in product(*axes):
            keys.add(key)
            if len(keys)>=cap: return cap
    return len(keys)
```
Note: keys of different lengths are distinct — but tuples of different lengths are distinct in a Python set anyway ✓.
